tier_rationale: Tentative only. Amazon operates a real cloud (Kindle Store, Send-to-Kindle, whispersync) and the device has Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Whether setup can be completed without an Amazon account on current firmware could not be confirmed from a qualifying source, which is the deciding fact between D2 and REJECT.
the_unplug_test: Not written. This record does not clear the evidence bar for a tier claim; publishing a confident unplug-test paragraph on unverified account-requirement facts would be exactly the guessed-field defect the project exists to avoid.

sources.supports: Amazon's own devices blog confirms the current entry-level Kindle at $109.99 with 16GB storage as a shipping model in the active lineup, alongside Paperwhite, Scribe and Colorsoft. Does not address account or registration requirements.

A user support thread describing an inability to find a way to bypass the Wi-Fi/registration screen on a recently purchased Kindle, suggesting no visible skip option in current firmware — but this is a single undated community post, not corroborated by a second independent source, and does not meet the evidence bar on its own.

open_questions: Does the current out-of-box setup wizard (2024/2025 firmware) offer any way to finish setup and reach the home/library screen without connecting to Wi-Fi and signing into an Amazon account? Older Kindle software (pre-2021 by most accounts) had a documented skip; it is unclear whether this still exists.

If registration can be skipped, does the device then function as a reader for personal, non-DRM documents transferred by USB/MTP with no account ever created — i.e. is the account requirement about the Kindle Store specifically, or about the device as a whole?

Amazon discontinued 'Download & Transfer via USB' for Kindle Store purchases in February 2025 (widely reported by TechRadar, Slickdeals and others) — does this same restriction affect personal-document sideloading, or only DRM store content?

Amazon's own support domain (amazon.com/gp/help/...) returned HTTP 503 to every automated fetch attempt during this research pass, which blocked direct confirmation from the highest-value primary source (the official Kindle setup guide). A researcher with browser access to amazon.com should check the setup guide and the Kindle Device Terms of Use directly.

This record intentionally has no tier claim confirmed. If setup is in fact account-mandatory on current hardware, this device should be republished as REJECT with a local-only-reading alternative cited (Kobo Clara Colour, already in this catalog, is the natural comparison point).
notes: Published despite inconclusive evidence because this is the single most-searched question in the e-reader category and a reader deserves an honest 'we don't know yet' over silence. The contrast case, Kobo Clara Colour (kobo-clara-colour), is fully verified at D2 with a documented account-free Sideloaded Mode shipped by Kobo itself — that record is the one to trust for a definitive account-free e-reader today. Amazon's help-center domain blocking automated access is itself notable: it made this the only device in this run where the manufacturer's own primary documentation could not be reached at all.

changelog.change: Published as insufficient_evidence: could not confirm from a qualifying source whether current Kindle setup can complete without an Amazon account.
